name: ired
desc: Minimalistic hexadecimal editor designed to be used in scripts
why: A tiny hex editor built for scripting binary patches, a close call that could still be fun for poking at binaries.

brief.what_it_is: ired is a small, minimalistic hexadecimal editor that is meant to be driven from scripts. It takes a binary file as input and lets you view it as hexdumps, search it for strings or hex pairs, seek to addresses, and write strings or hex bytes into it. It can also truncate or shrink the file, dump blocks to other files, and run shell commands. The package ships three executables: ired, vired, and bdiff. The README describes only the ired command language, so the vired and bdiff roles are not explained there.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says ired aims to be a minimalistic reimplementation of the radare shell, "without much complexity and relaying all the extensibility to external applications trying to keep the source as small as possible." It is named as the independent raw editor.
brief.how_it_works: ired reads a file into a current block and runs commands line by line against it, such as x for hexdump, w to write bytes or strings, s to seek, and b to set block size. The README describes a print command, p, with format letters for byte, word, dword, and qword, in both little and big endian, plus int32, float, zero-terminated strings, and skip. It notes that this print command is still a work in progress.

commands_seen.context: hexdump, per the README's command list 'x hexdump       hexdump'
hexpair dump, per the README's 'X dword dump    hexpair dump'
write a string, with a null terminator, into the current block
write hexpairs into the current block
set the block size (the README example uses 30)
get the file size, truncate the file to a size, or remove bytes
print formatted the current block, using the format letters listed in the README
run a command from the shell

brief.install_notes: The README gives no install steps beyond building from source. It says ired is known to build and run on GNU, Linux, OSX, Windows (mingw), cygwin, Solaris, and BSD. No runtime, account, or configuration requirements appear in the README. The Homebrew formula supplies bdiff, ired, and vired as executables.
brief.standout: It is a tiny hex editor built to be scripted rather than used interactively, and it pushes most extra features out to external programs. Its command language is a stripped-down take on the radare shell, which makes it a small, readable codebase to browse.
brief.status: quiet. The latest commit on master is dated Mar 21, 2021 ('Add more disassemblers and improve OpenWatcom support'). The most recent release referenced in the history is 'Release 0.6' on Dec 11, 2016. The README is labelled work in progress in places.
brief.caveats: The README marks the print command as work in progress. Math operations (+, -, *, /) are listed as TODO, and escaped characters in string write and search are also TODO. The README says the '.' command may be removed. Multiple commands on one line via ';' are only a TOTHINK item. The README gives no license text; the commit history mentions a MIT COPYING file added in 2019. The brew caveats field is empty.
